138:### Documentation style
139-
140-- Put the main point first, then the details (the pyramid principle).
141-- Use short sentences, the active voice, and the imperative for instructions ([ASD-STE100](https://www.asd-ste100.org/) where it applies).
142-- Write each fact in one place, and link to it from other places.
143-- Make sure that each claim agrees with the code. If possible, add a test.
144-
145-## CI workflows
146-
147-| Workflow | What it does |
148-|----------|--------------|
149-| [`ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml) | Runs `npm run check` on pushes and pull requests to `main`. On pull requests, the `commitlint` job checks the message of each commit with [`commitlint.config.js`](commitlint.config.js) |
150-| [`pi-assistant.yml`](.github/workflows/pi-assistant.yml) | Uses the action of this checkout to answer `@pi` requests in this repository. It acts as the `pi-action-agent` GitHub App (secrets `PI_APP_CLIENT_ID` and `PI_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`), so that pi can open pull requests and its pushes run CI |
151-| [`pi-direct-dogfood.yml`](.github/workflows/pi-direct-dogfood.yml) | `workflow_dispatch`: runs a direct prompt in `output` mode |
152-| [`pi-pr-review-dogfood.yml`](.github/workflows/pi-pr-review-dogfood.yml) | `workflow_dispatch`: reviews a pull request with `pr_number` in `output` mode |
153-
154-## Releases
155-
156-1. Make sure that `npm run check` passes on `main`.
157-2. Change `version` in `package.json`. Commit with the message `chore: release X.Y.Z`.
158-3. Tag the commit `vX.Y.Z`.
159-4. Move the major tag (`v2`) to the same commit. Users refer to the action as `cv/pi-action@v2`.
160-
161-## Pull requests
162-
163-1. Make a branch with a descriptive name, such as `feat/123-description`.
164-2. Write tests for new behavior.
165-3. Make sure that all hooks and `npm run check` pass.
166-4. Use Conventional Commits.
167-5. Keep the change small: one feature or one fix in each pull request.
168-6. Update the documentation when you add features or change behavior.

Use a `concurrency` group for each issue or pull request, with `cancel-in-progress: false`, as in the [quick start](../README.md#quick-start). Then runs on one thread do not overlap.

- **New comments join the running conversation.** pi-action looks for new `@pi` comments every `poll_interval` seconds (default 15) while pi works.
- **pi-action answers missed comments.** GitHub keeps only one pending run for each concurrency group, and cancels the others. Thus, a run answers each `@pi` comment on the thread that has no answer yet, not only the comment that started it.
- **pi-action posts each answer one time.** It records each posted answer and each posted failure in the thread. A later run does not post them again.

## Protection against conflicts

All pushes are fast-forward only.

- If two runs on one thread push at the same time, the remote rejects the later push. pi-action writes this to the log and does not overwrite the history of the other run. The run that was rejected stops pushing.
- pi-action retries other push failures (a network error, or `[remote rejected] ... (failed)` from GitHub) after 1, 3, and 10 seconds. If all retries fail, pi-action writes a warning to the log, and the next push tries again.

## Working-tree continuity

A thread also keeps the files that pi leaves uncommitted. Each run starts from a clean checkout. pi-action then restores the files as pi left them in the earlier run, staged and unstaged changes included. Thus, pi does not have to do its edits again after a question, a timeout, a cancellation, or a follow-up comment. To turn this off, set `worktree_snapshots: false`.

### What pi-action saves

pi-action saves a **snapshot** of the working tree after each model response and tool result, and at the end of the run. It saves a snapshot only when the files changed since the last snapshot. A snapshot contains:

- Changes to tracked files: modified, deleted, staged, and partially staged files, file modes (such as the executable bit), and symbolic links.
- Untracked files that git does not ignore.
- Commits that pi made but did not push. The snapshot is based on the commit that `HEAD` points to, so these commits stay available.
- Submodules as the commit that they point to, and Git LFS files as their pointers (not the contents).
